translations.text: And I said to you at that time, “I cannot bear the burden of you by myself.”
How, then, can I bear your weight, your burdens, and your disputes by myself?

Where are we going up? Our brothers have discouraged us and told us, “The people are greater, taller, and stronger than we are, and the cities are large and fortified up to the heavens. We also saw descendants of giants there.”

For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands and has known your journey through this wilderness. For these forty years the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.
From Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no town too strong for us. The Lord our God handed them all over to us.
We captured all his cities at that time, leaving no city that we did not take from them: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the territory of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
And the Arabah and the Jordan, with the boundary extending from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below Ashdod and Pisgah, on the height to the east.
Only leave your wives, your families, and your livestock—for I know that you have many possessions. Let them remain in your cities that I have given you.

Until the Lord gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too inherit the land that the Lord your God is giving you across the Jordan. Then you shall return, each to his inheritance that I have given you.
Do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God is the one who fights for you.
The Lord was angry with me because of you and did not listen to me. The Lord said to me, “Enough! Do not speak to me again about this matter.”
He made his covenant known to you and commanded you to carry out the ten commandments, and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
But the Lord brought you near and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his people and his inheritance, as you are today.
Be careful not to forget the covenant of the Lord your God that he made with you, and not to make for yourselves images and likenesses of anything concerning which the Lord your God commanded you.
The Lord will scatter you among the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the Lord your God scatters you.
There you will serve other gods, made by human hands, of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
Know today and take it to heart that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth below, and there is no other besides him.

Keep his laws and his commandments that I command you today, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, and so that you may live long in the land that the Lord your God is giving you for all time.
From Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon Valley, as far as Mount Sirion, which is Hermon.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the laws and judgments that I proclaim before you today, so that you may learn them, keep them, and carry them out.”

The seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall do no work—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the resident foreigner in your towns—so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your possessions.
Let these words that I command you today be on your heart.
And houses filled with every good thing that you did not fill, wells dug that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant; and you will eat and be satisfied.
But keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his testimonies, and his laws that he commanded you.
So that they do not turn your children away from me, and they serve other gods, and the LORD's anger burns against you and he quickly destroys you.
He repays those who hate him during their lifetime; he repays them by destroying them. He does not delay with those who hate him, but repays them during their lifetime.

Do not bring an unclean thing into your house, so that you do not become devoted to destruction like it. Instead, utterly reject it and regard it as utterly unclean, because it is devoted to destruction.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are entering to possess their land. Rather, it is because of the sins of these nations that the LORD your God destroys them before you, and to fulfill the promise he swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
I prayed before the LORD and said, 'LORD God, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.'
I made an ark of acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
The LORD said to me, 'Get up, set out, and go ahead of the people, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.'
The heavens and the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it, belong to the LORD your God.
Love the LORD your God and keep his requirements, his laws, his judgments, and his commandments all your days.

And what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their children, their tents, and everything they had, as they stood on their feet among all Israel.
Rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female slaves, and the Levites in your towns—because they have no inheritance or share with you.
When the LORD your God destroys the nations to whom you are going, and destroys them before you, and you take possession of them and settle in their land.
Be careful to carry out every command that I give you. Do not add to it or take away from it.
These you may eat from everything in the water: eat anything that has fins and scales.
And the stork and the heron according to their kinds, and the wild rooster and the peacock.
Do not abandon the Levite in your towns, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
Instead, open your hand to him and lend him whatever he lacks.
When you release him from your service as a free man, do not send him away empty-handed.

There must not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through fire, anyone who practices divination, anyone who performs illusions, anyone who interprets omens, or anyone who practices sorcery.
Listen, Israel! Today you are approaching battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart or be afraid. Do not tremble or panic before them.
If you do not want her, let her go free. Do not sell her for money or trade her, because you have humiliated her.
His father and mother shall seize him and bring him out to the elders of the town, to the gate of his home town.

When you come across a bird's nest along the road, in any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs, and the mother is sitting over the chicks or the eggs, do not take the mother along with her young.
The girl's father and mother shall take the evidence of the girl's virginity and bring it out to the elders of the town at the gate.

'Now he has made an accusation against her, saying, "I did not find your daughter to be a virgin." But here is the evidence of my daughter's virginity.' They shall spread out the cloth before the elders of the town.
Do not seek their peace or prosperity all the days of your life, forever.
Do not bring a prostitute’s earnings or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God to fulfill any vow, because both are unclean before the Lord your God.
If there is a dispute between a man and his neighbor, they must approach the judges, who will judge them, acquit the innocent, and condemn the guilty.

I have not eaten any of it during my mourning, nor removed any of it while I was unclean, nor set aside any of it for the dead. Instead, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God and done as you commanded me.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God is giving you, set up large stones for yourself and coat them with plaster.
But build the altar of the Lord your God with whole [?] stones, and offer whole burnt offerings on it before the Lord your God.
Sacrifice peace offerings and eat there, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
Moses commanded the people that day and said to them:
These will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife and uncovers his father’s nakedness. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
The Lord will send a plague upon you until he destroys you from the land you are entering to possess.
Your corpse will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and no one will frighten them away.
You will become engaged to a woman, but another man will marry her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not press wine from it.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
They will be signs and wonders upon you and your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart when you had an abundance of everything.
He will not give any of them any of the flesh of his children that he eats, because nothing will be left to him in the distress and hardship with which your enemy will afflict you in all your towns.
Unless you observe and carry out all the words of this law that are written in this book, and fear this glorious and awe-inspiring name of the Lord your God.
He will bring upon you all the plagues of the Egyptians that you fear, and they will cling to you.
The Lord’s anger burned against that land, bringing upon it all the curses written in this book.
The Lord your God will place all these curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate you and have persecuted you.
Moses commanded them and said to them: “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time in the year of release, at the Festival of Booths.”

For I will bring them into the land that I swore to their ancestors, flowing with milk and honey. They will eat, be satisfied, and live in luxury. They will turn aside to follow other gods and serve them, provoke me to anger, and break my covenant.
Is this how you repay the Lord, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father who made you his own? He made you and established you.
For their strength was not like our strength, and our enemies are judges.
Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eyesight had not grown dim, and his cheeks had not shriveled.
